import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1074

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1074](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1074)
-/

namespace Erdos1074

open scoped Nat
open Nat

/-- The EHS numbers (after Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao) are those $m\geq 1$ such that there
exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. -/
abbrev EHSNumbers : Set ℕ := {m | 1 ≤ m ∧ ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ ¬p ≡ 1 [MOD m] ∧ p ∣ m ! + 1}

/-- The Pillai primes are those primes $p$ such that there exists an $m \ge 1$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$-/
abbrev PillaiPrimes : Set ℕ := {p | p.Prime ∧ ∃ m ≥ 1, ¬p ≡ 1 [MOD m] ∧ p ∣ m ! + 1}

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem two_not_mem_pillaiPrimes : ¬ 2 ∈ PillaiPrimes := by
  norm_num
  intro m hm h
  exact (Nat.dvd_factorial (by decide) (hm.lt_of_ne (by bound))).modEq_zero_nat.add_right 1

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem twentyThree_mem_pillaiPrimes : 23 ∈ PillaiPrimes := by
  norm_num
  use 14
  decide

/-- Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. Does
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}
$$
exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, EHSNumbers.HasDensity c := by
  sorry

/-- Let $S$ be the set of all $m\geq 1$ such that there exists a prime $p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such
that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$. What is
$$
  \lim\frac{|S\cap[1, x]|}{x}?
$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.ii : EHSNumbers.HasDensity answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then does
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}
$$
exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c, PillaiPrimes.HasDensity c {p | p.Prime} := by
  sorry

/-- Similarly, if $P$ is the set of all primes $p$ such that there exists an $m$ with
$p\not\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ such that $m! + 1 \equiv 0\pmod{p}$, then what is
$$
  \lim\frac{|P\cap[1, x]|}{\pi(x)}?
$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.parts.iv :
    PillaiPrimes.HasDensity answer(sorry) {p | p.Prime} := by
  sorry

/-- Pillai [Pi30] raised the question of whether there exist any primes in $P$. This was answered
by Chowla, who noted that, for example, $14! + 1 \equiv 18! + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{23}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.mem_pillaiPrimes : 23 ∈ PillaiPrimes := by
  norm_num
  exact ⟨14, by decide⟩

/--
Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao proved that $S$ is infinite.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures/blob/3dec597bd1a73778760b761712a1fc5fb24bc5d7/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1074.lean#L99"]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_infinite : EHSNumbers.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős, Hardy, and Subbarao proved that $P$ is infinite. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.PillaiPrimes_infinite : PillaiPrimes.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- The sequence $S$ begins $8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, ...$ -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_init :
    nth EHSNumbers '' (Set.Icc 0 6) = {8, 9, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17} := by
  sorry

/-- The sequence $P$ begins $23, 29, 59, 61, 67, 71, ...$ -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.PillaiPrimes_init :
    nth PillaiPrimes '' (Set.Icc 0 5) = {23, 29, 59, 61, 67, 71} := by
  sorry

/-- Regarding the first question, Hardy and Subbarao computed all EHS numbers up to $2^{10}$, and
write "...if this trend conditions we expect [the limit] to be around 0.5, if it exists." -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_one_half : EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1074

findings.description: At line 126, `EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2)` asserts that the density exists and equals exactly 1/2. The cited passage only tentatively suggests a value 'around 0.5' if the finite-data trend continues and the limit exists. It then explicitly conjectures that the density exists and equals 1. The Lean variant turns the tentative numerical observation into a different exact conjecture and omits the source's actual density-one prediction. These predictions are incompatible by uniqueness of limits, which was checked in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: Hardy and Subbarao, 'A Modified Problem of Pillai and Some Related Questions', American Mathematical Monthly 109 (2002), Problem B, p. 557: 'The frequency with which the EHS numbers occur—most often in long sequences of consecutive integers—makes us believe that their asymptotic density exists and is unity. Erdős, though initially hesitant, later agreed with this view.' Appendix 4(i), p. 558, quotes Erdős's July 29, 1993 letter conjecturing the condition for 'almost all n'. See https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~subbarao/documents/2002_Pillai.pdf . The full quotation also appears at https://www.erdosproblems.com/1074 .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace this variant with the sourced conjecture `EHSNumbers.HasDensity 1`, renaming it appropriately and updating the docstring to quote the density-one prediction. Alternatively, remove the exact-half variant and retain the tentative finite-data observation only as commentary.

reformulations.difference: Here and in `Erdos1074.erdos_1074.parts.ii`, `HasDensity` counts natural numbers strictly below an integer cutoff n and divides by n, whereas the source counts the closed interval [1,x] with a real cutoff x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Zero is not an EHS number. Writing F(n)=|S∩[1,n]|, the Lean partial density at n+1 is F(n)/(n+1). Thus the closed-interval ratio F(n)/n has the same limit, since (n+1)/n tends to 1. For real x, the count equals F(floor x), and floor x/x tends to 1. The pointwise equivalence for every real density c was proved, including real cutoffs, in `/workspace/review/density-equivalence.lean` as `naturalDensity_iff_realClosed`; it preserves both existence and the requested value.

reformulations.difference: Here and in `Erdos1074.erdos_1074.parts.iv`, the relative-density definition counts primes strictly below an integer cutoff rather than using the source's closed-interval prime-counting denominator π(x).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: PillaiPrimes is a subset of the primes, so intersecting it with the reference set does not change the numerator. At cutoff n+1 the Lean ratio is exactly |P∩[1,n]|/π(n). Shifting the cutoff preserves convergence. For real x, both counts equal their values at floor x. The full equivalence for every real density c was proved in `/workspace/review/density-equivalence.lean` as `pillaiDensity_iff_realClosed`, preserving both the existence question and the numerical answer.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1074 — complete statement, commentary, and status; read through the Jina proxy with MathJax data-latex preserved.

https://www.math.ualberta.ca/~subbarao/documents/2002_Pillai.pdf — Hardy–Subbarao (2002), especially Definitions 2.9 and 2.11, Theorems 2.1 and 2.12, Problems A and B, and Appendix 4(i); text read through the Jina proxy.
https://oeis.org/A064164/internal — definition, initial terms, and primary-paper reference; read through the Jina proxy.
https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Pi30 — bibliography entry; the original question was read as quoted in Hardy–Subbarao.
review.notes: Checked all 14 declarations. Boundary checks cover zero, one, the initial zero denominators, and the necessarily bounded Pillai witness m<p. Computations reproduced the EHS prefix through 18 and Pillai primes below 100; all Pillai membership cases through 71 were also kernel-checked. Nat.nth is zero-indexed, so the initial-sequence statements have the correct lengths and ordering. The exact cited EHS infinitude proof replayed successfully with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The source still records the density questions as open. OEIS A063980 could not be fetched, but its relevant definition and initial terms were independently verified against the primary paper and Lean computations. Experiments are under /workspace/review; the target file was not changed.

not_demonstrated.reason: The discrepancy concerns which limiting value the source conjectures. The review supplies no short proof of `Erdos1074.EHSNumbers.HasDensity (1 / 2)` or its negation. Uniqueness of limits only shows incompatibility with density 1; assuming the source's unproved density-one conjecture would not be an unconditional disproof of the declaration.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created. The source-fidelity finding does not provide a trivial proof or disproof of the formalized statement.
submission.gave_up_reason: Neither the exact-half density assertion nor its negation admits a short, honest proof established by this review. A conditional incompatibility argument would not meet the requirement to demonstrate the statement as formalized.

submission.summary: Replaced the exact-half density assertion with the sourced conjecture EHSNumbers.HasDensity 1, renaming the declaration to Erdos1074.erdos_1074.variants.EHSNumbers_density_one. Updated its docstring to quote Hardy and Subbarao's density-one prediction while preserving the research-open and AMS attributes. Only the reported declaration and its docstring were changed; compilation reports no errors and only expected declaration-uses-sorry warnings.
